title: negotiator-mnemonics-and-case-notes
content:
Negotiation Mnemonics & Case Notes — personal scratchpad

PURPOSE: quick mental model + bite-sized fallback language for 1:1 redlines. Keep short, use in sync calls. This is intentionally messy.

Top-level mnemonic: SPARC
- S = Security (incident notification, breach scope, encryption, MFA, pen tests)
- P = Privacy & Data (PII classification, retention windows, export rights, inference/derived data)
- A = Access & Audit (who, how, logging, admin console access)
- R = Rights & Results (IP, model output ownership, use restrictions, sublicensing)
- C = Continuity & Credits (SLA, termination & transition, escrow/exports)

Use SPARC as triage during a redline skim: flag anything that touches these areas and add severity tag (S1,S2,S3).

Quick severity guide (mental):
- S1: product-blocker or legal/regulatory risk (data residency, export ban, litigation exposure)
- S2: operational risk that increases TCO or latency to ship (excessive audit rights, throttling)
- S3: negotiation polish items (notice periods, vague definitions)

Sample one-liners to surface in syncs / slack summaries:
- "Flagging sec/privacy as S1 — need to fix notification timeline + encryption SAAS wording."
- "Customer asked for model-output IP carveout; propose narrow term-limited license instead of assignment."
- "Ops: watch for admin console entitlements — propose limited view w/ audit log only."

Redline battle cards (short alternatives to propose quickly)
1) Security incident notification
- Ask: 72 hours + summary + mitigation plan (reasonable efforts).
- Counter (if customer pushes 24h): 48 hours for confirmed incidents; 72 for suspected; we keep them updated.
- Preferred redline snippet (quick): "Supplier will notify Customer of confirmed security incidents affecting Customer Data within 48 hours of confirmation and provide regular remediation updates until resolved. For suspected incidents, initial notification within 72 hours on a best-efforts basis."
- Notes: don't commit to forensic root-cause within X days; avoid accepting pen-test remediation SLAs unless scoped.

2) Data export / model-output IP
- Common ask = customer wants all outputs assigned. Push back: offer a perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free license to use outputs for the agreed use-case, limited to Customer Data and not training Supplier models.
- Alternative language (fast): "Customer is granted a perpetual, non-exclusive, non-transferable license to use Model Outputs for its internal business purposes; Supplier retains all underlying model and tooling IP. Customer may not use outputs to reproduce or train alternative models without Supplier's prior consent."
- If they insist on assignment: ask for narrow scope (single workspace, specific dataset IDs) + compensation.

3) Subprocessor / subcontractor visibility
- If customer wants pre-approval: offer 30-day notice + right to terminate for data residency violations. Do not accept blanket pre-approval of all subprocessors.
- Fast counter: "Supplier will maintain a list of subprocessors and provide notice of material changes; Customer may terminate for cause if a change materially violates data residency or regulatory requirements."

4) SLA credits table (simplified)
- Latency SLOs: P99 or request-based (we rarely commit P99 without Dedicated).
- Availability: propose 99.5% for hosted; 99.9% for Dedicated (negotiable).
- Credit ladder (example): <99.5% = 5% credit; <99% = 15%; <95% = 30% or termination right after cure period.
- Notes: preserve exclude windows (maintenance, force majeure, customer's misconfiguration).

5) Termination & transition
- Ask for 90-day export window with standard export formats and customer-managed KMS option for private deployments.
- Fast clause: "Upon termination Customer may export Customer Data for 90 days; Supplier will provide reasonable assistance to export in machine-readable format. After 90 days Supplier may delete remaining data unless an alternative retention arrangement is agreed."
- Avoid: open-ended escrow obligations or long-term storage guarantees.

Concession ladder (how I personally drive to a deal):
- Stage 0 (initial ask): capture them in trackable comments in the doc.
- Stage 1 (acceptable compromise): narrow scope + timebox + audit trail (e.g., license vs assignment; 90-day export).
- Stage 2 (last resort): offer compensating controls + paid premium (additional fee for bespoke data residency).
- Stage 3 (walkaway): client insists on model/training assignment, unlimited audit w/o NDA protections, or indefinite data escrow at Supplier cost.

Negotiation micro-scripts (short, usable in calls)
- When pushed on assignment: "We can offer a very strong license for your outputs that gives you full operational control for your use cases. Assignment of underlying model IP is a different commercial proposition — if that's a hard requirement we should scope it as a paid custom work item."
- When asked for 24h breach notice: "We understand urgency; we commit to confirmed incident notification within 48 hours and continuous remediation updates — that'll give us time to verify and avoid false positives."
- When asked for pre-approval of subprocessors: "We maintain a public list and will notify material changes. If a change materially affects your compliance posture, you have termination for cause — we think that's reasonable tradeoff for operational flexibility."

Notes to self / TODOs (short)
- Confirm with security whether 48h confirmed vs 72h suspected is acceptable (sec-approved threshold).
- Add standard language for KMS BYOK (private) and who covers HSM costs.
- Draft one-liner for model-output license vs assignment that Sales can include in initial offers.
- Check precedent: RINF-1122 (customer X carveout) — see linked_artifacts.

Edge cases / red flags to escalate immediately
- Customer asks to hold raw training data or model weights — escalate to Product & Applied ML (high risk).
- Legal wants unlimited right to audit infra including live request payloads w/o scoped redaction — escalate (SRE + Product).
- Customer demands developer-level console access for their vendor ops team — consider scoped read-only + IP protections.

Mini checklist for a rushed redline review (2–3 mins)
1) Does it touch SPARC? (quick scan)
2) Any absolute takedowns (assignment of core model IP, indefinite escrow at Supplier expense, unlimited audit)? If yes, escalate.
3) Are timelines realistic (incident, export window)? push to standards above.
4) Are credits/termination proportional to impact? don't accept unlimited termination triggers tied to ambiguous "material breach".

Personal heuristics (why I push back)
- Avoid vague or undefined obligations that create operational commitments we can't quantify.
- Prefer timeboxes and measurable windows (48/72/90 days) over qualifiers like "promptly" or "reasonable efforts" without context — but "reasonable efforts" can remain for remediation descriptions.
- Protect core model IP and the right to improve models (no training on customer outputs unless contracted).

Quick redline snippets I keep copying (one-liners)
- Incident: "notify within 48 hours for confirmed incidents; 72 for suspected; updates every 3 business days until resolved."
- Export: "export support for 90 days in machine-readable, documented format; assistance subject to professional services rates beyond 8 hours."
- IP: "Supplier retains all rights in models; Customer receives a perpetual license to Model Outputs for internal business use only; no rights to retrain Supplier models."

Unresolved questions to raise in legal sync:
- Can we standardize 48h confirmed / 72h suspected across hosted + dedicated? (ops impact)
- When do we accept assignment vs license for outputs? thresholds (deal size, strategic partner).
- Default SLA percentages for small deals (<$10k/mo) vs committed capacity.

Last bits (notes to self style)
- Keep this doc short and copy-paste friendly. Maintain a separate "sign-off snippets" doc for sales templates.
- Remove PII from example clauses before sharing externally.
- If negotiating with regulated industry (health/finance), pre-load BAA / DPA clause templates and ask for early security questionnaire (SIG).

-- end scratchpad --

(half-formed thoughts below; keep for brainstorming)
- Could introduce a second mnemonic for commercial tradeoffs: PRICE = Pricing floor, Residuals (IP), Insurance, Credits, Exclusivity — helps when structuring concession ladders.
- Add a short cheat sheet for "how to ask for a little money for risky concessions" (e.g., training/data use for model improvements => charge premium + opt-out).
summary: Personal scratchpad with mnemonic SPARC to triage redlines, quick fallback language for security/privacy/SLA/IP/export, concession ladder and micro-scripts, todo list and escalation flags.
